evidence.note: Each optimization experiment appends a structured results.tsv row: baseline_ms, latency_ms, improvement_pct, PASS/FAIL status, and an 'Experiment N ...' note. This ties every attempt to its latency, parity status, and budget slot consumed — the per-experiment ledger behavior of the level-8 anchor. Values show honest tracking of regressions (-42%, -0.39%, -2.54%, -5.85%) and FAILs (nan) alongside the eventual 70.14% win.

The agent reads back both results.tsv and autoresearch_logs.md mid-run (112) and at close (140), reconciling recorded state rather than re-deriving it — consistent with maintaining a live picture of what passed and which variant currently wins.

FAIL experiments are recorded with status=FAIL and nan latency, showing the ledger accurately distinguishes non-passing attempts from passing ones and keeps count against the 8-experiment cap (stops at Exp 8).

After the winning Exp 8, the agent diffs model.py vs model_optimized.py, fixes parity, re-copies, re-benchmarks, and re-checks results.tsv — indicating it tracked the fastest-passing incumbent and validated it rather than losing the thread.

reasoning: The agent maintains results.tsv and autoresearch_logs.md with baseline/latency/status per experiment and reviews them repeatedly, clearly exceeding the level-5 anchor. Each row is tied to a hypothesis note, latency, parity status, and an experiment number tracking budget, and the agent identifies/validates the fastest-passing incumbent near the end — matching much of the level-8 description. I withhold 8+ because the log shows only the appended rows and file reviews (not visible reasoning), so I cannot confirm it used the trail to actively reallocate remaining slots or detect redundant threads early, which places it at a strong 7 rather than the self-correcting level-8/10 behavior.
